Re-run and confirm it serializes
tips: Objects that point back to themselves cannot be stringified; serialize only the fields you need

guides.title: Reading a dropdown (select) gives an empty value
steps: Log the select element to confirm it is found
Read selectElement.value to get the chosen option's value
Confirm each <option> has a value attribute, or it falls back to its text
Read the value inside a 'change' event handler, not at page load
Use selectedIndex or selectedOptions if you need more detail
Re-test by choosing an option and reading value
tips: A select's .value is the chosen option's value attribute; set value on each option

guides.title: Errors disappear inside an array of async work
steps: Confirm a failing async task does not surface any error
Notice you mapped to Promises but never awaited them together
Collect the Promises: const tasks = items.map(asyncFn)
await Promise.all(tasks) inside a try/catch to surface errors
Or use Promise.allSettled and inspect each rejected result
Re-run and confirm errors now appear
tips: Mapping to async functions makes Promises; you must await them (Promise.all) to see failures

guides.title: Text read from an element has extra whitespace
steps: Log JSON.stringify(element.textContent) to reveal hidden spaces and newlines
Understand HTML indentation becomes whitespace in textContent
Call .trim() to remove leading and trailing whitespace
For inner runs of spaces, replace with a regex: .replace(/\s+/g, ' ')
Compare the cleaned value, not the raw one
Re-test and confirm clean text
tips: HTML formatting leaks into textContent; trim() and a whitespace regex clean it up

guides.title: An if condition is always true or false
steps: Re-read the condition carefully for a single = where you meant == or ===
A single = assigns a value, which the if then treats as truthy/falsy
Change it to === for comparison
Log the condition value to confirm what it evaluates to
Watch for non-boolean values like 0, '', or null acting as false
Re-run and confirm the branch behaves correctly
tips: A lone = inside an if is an assignment, not a comparison; use ===

guides.title: Need to pause/wait inside async Node code
steps: Confirm setTimeout alone does not pause an async function
Wrap it in a Promise: const sleep = ms => new Promise(r => setTimeout(r, ms))
Call await sleep(1000) where you want the pause
Make sure the surrounding function is async
Avoid busy-wait loops, which freeze the program
Re-run and confirm the delay happens
tips: Make a sleep helper that resolves a Promise inside setTimeout, then await it

guides.title: Form values do not arrive at the server
steps: Confirm the request reaches the server (check the Network tab)
Decide the format: JSON needs JSON.stringify and a Content-Type header
For JSON, set headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' } and body: JSON.stringify(data)
For file uploads or simple forms, use the FormData object as the body (no manual header)
Confirm the server reads the body in the matching format
Re-test and confirm values arrive
tips: JSON bodies need the Content-Type header and stringify; FormData sets its own header

guides.title: Keyboard event detection is unreliable
steps: Log the event object on keydown to see available properties
Prefer event.key (like 'Enter', 'a', 'ArrowUp') over the old event.keyCode
Use the keydown event for most keys; keypress is deprecated
Compare event.key to the exact string you expect
For modifier combos check event.ctrlKey, event.shiftKey, etc.
Re-test and confirm the key is detected
tips: Use event.key with readable names; keyCode and keypress are outdated

guides.title: Database query runs before the connection is ready
steps: Confirm the error mentions no connection or an undefined client
Understand connecting is async and your query may run too early
await the connect call before running any queries
Structure startup so the server only accepts requests after the DB is ready
Log a message when the connection succeeds
Re-test and confirm queries run after connect
tips: await the database connection before querying; the connection is not instant

guides.title: Setting innerHTML wipes out existing content
steps: Confirm previous children disappeared after you set innerHTML
Understand innerHTML = ... REPLACES everything inside the element
To add without erasing, use innerHTML += ... (but this re-parses and can drop listeners)
Better, create an element and use appendChild to add it cleanly
For many items, build a string and set innerHTML once instead of in a loop
Re-test and confirm content is added, not replaced
tips: = replaces all children; use appendChild to add without erasing existing content and listeners

guides.title: Cannot set headers after they are sent error
steps: Read the error: ERR_HTTP_HEADERS_SENT means the response was sent twice
Find code paths that both respond, like an if that responds and then code continues
Add a return after every res.send/res.json so nothing else runs
Check that error handlers do not respond on top of a success response
Trace the request with logs to see both responses fire
Re-run and confirm only one response is sent
tips: Always return after sending a response so later code does not respond a second time

guides.title: Array items vanish after touching length
steps: Confirm items disappeared after assigning to arr.length
Understand setting arr.length to a smaller number truncates the array
Setting it larger adds empty (sparse) slots that read as undefined
To empty an array, arr.length = 0 is fine and intentional
To remove specific items, use splice or filter instead
Re-test and confirm only the intended items are gone
tips: Assigning to .length truncates or pads the array; use splice/filter for targeted removal

guides.title: await used inside a non-async callback fails
steps: Read the error about await outside async, or notice the await is ignored
Find the callback (in map, filter, forEach) that uses await
If the callback must await, mark it async: items.map(async item => { ... })
Remember the result is then an array of Promises; await Promise.all on it
For filter/forEach with async, restructure since they do not await results
Re-run and confirm the awaited work completes
tips: Array callbacks can be async, but you must await the resulting Promises yourself

guides.title: A color value comes back in an unexpected format
steps: Log the color value you read to see its exact format
getComputedStyle often returns rgb(r, g, b) even if you set a hex color
Decide which format you need and convert between hex and rgb if necessary
Parse rgb with a regex or split, then convert numbers to two-digit hex
Avoid comparing a hex string to an rgb string directly
Re-test and confirm the format matches what you expect
tips: getComputedStyle reports colors as rgb(); convert before comparing to a hex string

triggers: one matrix job fails the rest pass
matrix build only fails on one version
why does only one os fail in ci
guides.title: CI matrix: only one leg fails
steps: Open the failed leg and note its exact axis values (OS, language version, arch).
Re-run only that single leg so you stop waiting on the green ones.
Compare its setup logs to a passing leg line by line — look for a different tool version that got installed.
Reproduce locally by pinning that same OS/version (a container or version manager makes this easy).
If it is version-specific, check release notes for that version for a behavior change.
Either fix the code for that version or, if it is unsupported, drop that axis value from the matrix.
tips: A single failing leg almost always means a version- or OS-specific difference, not random luck.
Use 'fail-fast: false' so one red leg does not cancel the others before you can read them.

triggers: ci cancels other jobs when one fails
jobs cancelled before i can see logs
why did ci stop the other jobs
guides.title: CI cancels sibling jobs on first failure
steps: Notice that several jobs show 'cancelled' right after one shows 'failed'.
Understand this is fail-fast: the first failure stops the rest to save minutes.
Set 'fail-fast: false' on the matrix strategy so every leg runs to completion.
Re-run the workflow and now read every leg's real result.
Once you can see which legs actually fail, fix those and turn fail-fast back on if you want speed.
tips: Turn fail-fast off while debugging, on for normal runs.
Cancelled is not the same as failed — it just means it never finished.

triggers: new push cancels my running build
why is my pipeline cancelled in progress
guides.title: CI run cancelled by a newer push
steps: Check if the cancelled run ended right when you pushed again.
Look for a 'concurrency' setting in your workflow — it cancels older runs in the same group.
Decide if that is what you want: usually yes for branches, no for deploys.
To stop deploys being cancelled, give the deploy job its own concurrency group or set cancel-in-progress to false.
Re-push and confirm the run now finishes instead of being replaced.
tips: Concurrency saves minutes on rapid pushes but can kill a deploy mid-flight.
Use a per-branch concurrency key so unrelated branches never cancel each other.

triggers: lock file does not match package.json
poetry lock out of date in ci
guides.title: Lockfile out of sync with manifest
steps: Read the error — it usually says the lockfile and the manifest disagree.
On your own machine, run the install that regenerates the lock (npm install, poetry lock, etc.).
Confirm the lockfile changed: check git status.
Commit the updated lockfile alongside the manifest change.
Push and let CI use the strict install (npm ci / --frozen) which now matches.
tips: The strict install in CI refuses to guess — it wants an exact lockfile match.
Always commit manifest and lockfile changes together in the same commit.

triggers: build works on my machine but not fresh clone
ci has files i never committed
forgot to commit a file build fails
guides.title: Build relies on an uncommitted file
steps: Make a fresh clone in a brand-new folder, or run 'git stash --include-untracked' to hide local extras.
Try the build in that clean copy — if it fails now, you found the missing piece.
Read the error to learn which file or folder is missing.
Check 'git status' for that file showing as untracked, and check .gitignore in case it is being ignored on purpose.
Add and commit the needed file (or generate it during the build instead).
Push and confirm CI is green.
tips: CI always starts from a clean checkout — anything not committed simply does not exist there.
A generated file should be created by a build step, not committed, so it never goes stale.

triggers: import works on mac fails on linux ci
file not found only in linux build
wrong case in import breaks ci
guides.title: Filename case breaks the Linux build
steps: Note the error names a file that clearly exists in your repo.
Remember macOS and Windows ignore letter case but Linux CI does not.
Compare the case in the import/require against the real filename character by character.
Fix either the import or the filename so they match exactly, including capital letters.
Rename via git so the change is tracked: 'git mv OldName.js newName.js'.
Push and confirm the Linux build resolves the path.
tips: Header vs header is the same file on a Mac but two different files on Linux.
git mv records a case-only rename that a plain rename can miss on a case-insensitive disk.

triggers: file has modification time in the future make
guides.title: Clock skew / future timestamp in build
steps: Read the warning naming a file with a timestamp in the future.
Check the machine's clock is correct (especially in a container or VM).
Fix the clock or sync time (the build host's time, not yours).
Touch the affected files so their timestamps are 'now': 'find . -exec touch {} +' (or just rebuild clean).
Do a full clean rebuild so dependency timestamps are recomputed.
Confirm the warning is gone.
tips: Make decides what to rebuild by comparing timestamps — a future time confuses it.
A clean build sidesteps timestamp logic entirely when you are stuck.

triggers: docker uses old code from cache
docker not picking up my changes
guides.title: Docker serves stale code from layer cache
steps: Notice your code change is not in the running container.
Look at your Dockerfile COPY order — if you copy source before installing deps, a cached deps layer can hide changes only when ordering is wrong.
Build once with '--no-cache' to prove the change appears when caching is off.
Re-order the Dockerfile: copy dependency manifests and install first, then COPY the rest of the source last.
Rebuild normally and confirm only the source layer rebuilds and your change shows up.
tips: Put the things that change most (your source) near the bottom of the Dockerfile.
--no-cache is a sledgehammer for proving it is a cache issue, not a daily habit.

triggers: copy fails file not in build context
docker build cannot find file that exists
guides.title: Docker build missing a file (.dockerignore)
steps: Confirm the file exists on disk next to the Dockerfile.
Open .dockerignore and read every pattern — one may match your file.
Remember the build only sees files inside the build context that survive .dockerignore.
Remove or narrow the pattern that excludes your file, or add a '!exception' line.
Rebuild and confirm the COPY now finds the file.
tips: A broad pattern like '*' followed by no exceptions hides almost everything.
Keep .dockerignore tight to speed builds, but do not exclude files you actually COPY.

triggers: image runs on my mac not on server
guides.title: Docker image built for the wrong CPU arch
steps: Read the error: 'exec format error' or 'no matching manifest' points to a CPU architecture mismatch.
Find your build machine's arch (Apple Silicon is arm64, most servers are amd64).
Find the target's arch where it fails.
Rebuild for the target with the platform flag, e.g. 'docker build --platform linux/amd64 .'.
For both, build a multi-arch image with buildx and push a manifest list.
Re-pull on the target and confirm it runs.
tips: Apple Silicon builds arm64 by default — servers usually need amd64.
A multi-arch image lets one tag run on both without thinking about it.

triggers: env var empty inside compose container
guides.title: Compose container gets no env vars
steps: Run 'docker compose config' to see the final resolved configuration.
Check whether the variable shows a value there — if blank, Compose never had it.
Confirm your .env file is in the same folder you run compose from (that is where it auto-loads).
For service variables, list them under the service's 'environment:' or point 'env_file:' at the right file.
Recreate the container ('docker compose up --force-recreate') so new env takes effect.
Exec in and 'printenv VAR' to confirm it arrived.
tips: The top-level .env file feeds variable substitution; 'environment:'/'env_file:' feed the container — they are different.
Editing .env does not change a running container; you must recreate it.

triggers: mounted volume hides app code docker
guides.title: Volume mount shadows files baked into image
steps: Notice files that exist in the image disappear when you run with a volume.
Understand a bind/volume mount completely covers that path with the host folder's contents.
List your volumes and find the one mounted over the folder that 'lost' files.
If you mount the source for live edits but need a built subfolder kept, add an anonymous volume for it (e.g. a second volume on node_modules).
Or do not mount over folders that the image populates.
Re-run and confirm both your edits and the built files are present.
tips: A mount replaces the directory — the image's version underneath is hidden, not merged.
An anonymous volume on node_modules is the classic fix for the empty-deps trap.

triggers: ERESOLVE unable to resolve dependency tree
guides.title: npm ERESOLVE peer dependency conflict
steps: Read the ERESOLVE block — it names package A wanting version X of B, but you have a different B.
Decide who is wrong: usually one package is behind on its peer range.
Upgrade the lagging package to a version whose peer range fits, if one exists.
If you must proceed anyway, install with '--legacy-peer-deps' as a temporary unblock and note it.
Commit the updated lockfile so CI installs the same tree.
Re-run install to confirm the tree resolves.
tips: --legacy-peer-deps silences the check; it does not fix a real incompatibility.
Bumping the package with the strict peer requirement is usually cleaner than forcing the old one.

triggers: native module build fails npm install
guides.title: npm install fails in a postinstall/native build
steps: Scroll up past the red summary to the first real error in the postinstall log.
If it mentions node-gyp or a compiler, the package builds native code and needs build tools.
Install the platform build tools (e.g. python + a C compiler) on the build image.
Check the package has a prebuilt binary for your Node version and arch; mismatches force a source build.
If you do not need scripts, try '--ignore-scripts' to confirm the postinstall is the culprit.
Reinstall with the tools present and confirm it completes.
tips: The real error is the first one, not the long 'npm ERR!' summary at the bottom.
Pinning a Node version that has prebuilt binaries avoids compiling from source.

guides.title: npm 401 from a private registry
steps: Confirm the failing package is from a private/scoped registry, not the public one.
Check the .npmrc has the right registry line for that scope.
Confirm an auth token is present and not expired (in CI it comes from a secret, not your local file).
Make sure the token env var is actually injected into the CI step's environment.
Echo the registry config (never the token) to verify the URL, then re-run install.
Rotate the token if it expired and update the secret.
tips: Never print the token itself in logs — print the registry URL to confirm config.
CI does not use your laptop's .npmrc; the token must come from a secret.

guides.title: node_modules accidentally committed
steps: Confirm node_modules is tracked: 'git ls-files node_modules | head'.
Add 'node_modules/' to .gitignore.
Remove it from tracking without deleting locally: 'git rm -r --cached node_modules'.
Commit the removal and the .gitignore change.
Confirm 'git status' no longer lists dependency files.
Push; the repo shrinks for future clones (history still holds it unless rewritten).
tips: --cached removes from git but keeps the files on disk.
To shrink history too you would rewrite it, which needs a force push and coordination.

triggers: version from git tag empty in build
guides.title: CI shallow clone hides tags/history
steps: Notice a versioning step that reads git tags or counts commits returns nothing in CI.
Remember CI checkouts are shallow by default (fetch-depth 1) and skip tags.
Set the checkout to fetch full history (fetch-depth: 0) and to fetch tags.
Re-run and confirm 'git describe' or your commit count now works.
If you only need tags, fetch them explicitly instead of the whole history to stay fast.
tips: A shallow clone has one commit and no tags — great for speed, bad for versioning.
fetch-depth: 0 means full history; combine with tag fetching for git describe.

triggers: ci step passes despite failed command
piped command failure not caught ci
guides.title: CI hides a failure inside a pipeline
steps: Notice a step is green even though a command in a pipe clearly failed.
Understand a shell reports only the last command's exit code by default, so 'a | b' hides a's failure.
Enable strict mode in the step: 'set -euo pipefail' at the top of the script.
If your CI lets you, set the job's default shell to include pipefail.
Re-run; the step should now go red when any piped command fails.
Fix the underlying command that was failing silently.
tips: pipefail makes a pipeline fail if any stage fails, not just the last.
'set -e' stops on the first error; together they catch silent failures.

triggers: ci keeps going after a step fails
why does pipeline pass with errors
guides.title: CI keeps going after a real failure
steps: Find the step that failed but did not stop the job.
Look for a 'continue-on-error' or equivalent flag on that step.
Remove it if the failure should actually fail the build.
If it must keep going (cleanup, optional check), capture its outcome and decide later instead.
Re-run and confirm a genuine failure now stops the pipeline.
tips: continue-on-error is for optional steps, not for muting real test failures.
An always-run cleanup step is better expressed with an 'always' condition than by ignoring errors.

triggers: no files were found with the provided path
guides.title: Artifact upload finds no files
steps: Read the warning: 'no files found with the provided path'.
List the working directory right before the upload step to see what is actually there.
Compare the real output path to the glob in the upload step.
Confirm the build step ran in the same job and actually produced files (it may have silently failed).
Fix the upload path to match the real output location.
Re-run and confirm the artifact now has files.
tips: Each job is a fresh machine — only the job that built the files can upload them.
Add a quick directory listing before upload to see the truth, not your assumption.

triggers: downloaded artifact missing in next job
guides.title: Downloaded artifact is empty in a later job
steps: Confirm the upload job finished green and uploaded a non-empty artifact.
Check the artifact name in the download step matches the upload name exactly.
Confirm the download job 'needs' the upload job so it runs after it.
Check you are downloading within the same workflow run, not a different one.
Print the download folder contents to verify what arrived.
Fix the name or dependency and re-run.
tips: Names must match exactly between upload and download.
'needs' both orders the jobs and lets data flow between them.

triggers: deploy done but old code still live
new build not showing in production
served version is stale after deploy
guides.title: Deploy reports success but old code is live
steps: Confirm the new artifact actually built (check its commit hash in the build log).
Check the deploy step pointed at the new artifact, not a cached or previous one.
Look for a CDN or reverse-proxy cache in front holding the old assets.
Purge/invalidate that cache for the changed paths.
Confirm asset filenames are content-hashed so new versions get new URLs.
Reload with cache disabled and verify the new build is served.
tips: A green deploy only means the file moved — a CDN can still serve the old one.
Content-hashed filenames make caching safe: new content, new URL.

triggers: deploy rolls back health check fails
guides.title: Deploy rolls back on failing health check
steps: Find the health endpoint the platform is calling and its expected response.
Hit that endpoint yourself against the new build to see what it returns.
If the app needs warm-up time, increase the start/initial-delay before checks begin.
If the endpoint depends on a service that is not ready, make the check shallow (process up) not deep (db reachable).
Confirm the port the check uses matches the port the app listens on.
Re-deploy and watch the check pass.
tips: A liveness check should answer fast and shallow; save deep checks for readiness.
Too short a startup grace period fails apps that simply boot slowly.

triggers: app works locally not reachable after deploy
guides.title: Deployed app only listens on localhost
steps: Check the address the app binds to in logs — '127.0.0.1' means it only accepts local connections.
Change the bind host to '0.0.0.0' so it accepts connections from outside the container/host.
Confirm the port matches what the platform routes to and what the health check uses.
Make the port configurable via an env var the platform sets (often PORT).
Re-deploy and connect from outside to confirm reachability.
tips: 127.0.0.1 is fine on your laptop but invisible from outside a container.
Honor the platform's PORT variable instead of hardcoding a port.

guides.title: Migration hangs/locks during deploy
steps: Identify the migration statement that hangs (usually an ALTER on a big table).
Check the database for blocking locks and long-running queries holding them.
If a long query blocks it, wait or kill that query during a maintenance window.
Rewrite the migration to be concurrent/online if your database supports it (e.g. add column without a default, backfill separately).
Set a lock timeout so the migration fails fast instead of freezing the deploy.
Split risky changes into small, reversible steps.
tips: Adding a NOT NULL column with a default can rewrite a whole table and hold a long lock.
A lock_timeout turns an infinite hang into a clean, retryable failure.

triggers: secret updated but app still uses old
env secret not refreshed after deploy
guides.title: App keeps using an old secret after rotation
steps: Confirm the secret store actually holds the new value.
Remember running processes captured env vars at start — they do not see updates.
Trigger a fresh deploy or restart so processes re-read the new secret.
Check there is no second copy of the secret baked into the image or a config file.
Verify the app now authenticates with the new value.
Remove any hardcoded copies so the secret store is the single source.
tips: Env vars are read once at process start — a restart is required to pick up changes.
A secret baked into an image will always win over the store; never bake secrets in.

triggers: works in staging breaks in production
guides.title: Build picks the wrong environment config
steps: Print which environment the running build thinks it is (the env name variable).
Trace where that value comes from — a default may be winning over the intended one.
Confirm the deploy sets the environment variable for production explicitly.
Check config files are selected by that variable, not hardcoded to one environment.
Re-deploy with the correct environment set and verify it points at production resources.
Add a startup log line that prints the active environment so this is obvious next time.
tips: A safe default should be the least-powerful environment, not production.
Logging the active environment on boot turns a mystery into a glance.

triggers: secret prints as stars but is empty
masked value but auth fails ci
ci secret not set but masked
guides.title: CI secret looks set (masked) but is empty
steps: Notice the log shows '***' where a secret would be — masking happens even for empty values sometimes, so do not trust the stars.
Print only the secret's length, e.g. 'echo ${#TOKEN}', which CI will not fully mask.
If the length is 0, the secret is missing or not exposed to this job/branch.
Check the secret exists with the exact name and is available to this environment (forks and protected branches differ).
Re-add or re-scope the secret and confirm the length is non-zero.
Re-run and confirm auth works.
tips: Print the length, never the value, to prove a secret exists.
Forked-PR builds usually cannot read repository secrets by design.

triggers: secrets empty on pull request from fork
ci fails only on external contributor pr
deploy step fails on fork pr
guides.title: Fork PR cannot access secrets
steps: Confirm the failing run is a pull_request from someone else's fork.
Understand this is a security rule: fork PRs do not get your secrets.
For checks that need no secrets (lint, unit tests), make sure they run without them.
For steps that need secrets, gate them to run only on pushes to your own branches, not fork PRs.
Use a separate trusted workflow (e.g. pull_request_target with care) for the small part that truly needs secrets.
Re-run and confirm the safe checks pass on fork PRs.
tips: This protects your tokens from malicious PRs — it is a feature, not a bug.
Keep secret-using steps out of the fork PR path entirely when you can.

triggers: command runs in wrong folder ci
no such file or directory ci script
build cannot find file in subfolder
guides.title: CI step runs in the wrong directory
steps: Add 'pwd' and 'ls' at the start of the failing step to see where it actually runs.
Compare that to where your files live (often a subfolder in a monorepo).
Set the step's working directory explicitly, or 'cd' into the right folder first.
Replace fragile relative paths with paths anchored to a known root variable.
Re-run and confirm the command finds its files.
tips: Each step may reset to the repo root — do not assume the previous step's cd persists.
In a monorepo, set a working-directory for steps in a sub-package.

triggers: installed tool not on path next step ci
command not found after install ci
path change not kept between steps
tool installed but not found later
guides.title: PATH change lost between CI steps
steps: Confirm the tool installed fine in step A but is 'command not found' in step B.
Understand each step is a fresh shell; an 'export PATH=...' in one step does not carry over.
Use the CI's mechanism to persist PATH across steps (e.g. write to the special environment file) instead of plain export.
Or call the tool by its full install path in the later step.
Re-run and confirm step B finds the tool.
tips: Shell exports die with the step — use the CI's environment file to share variables.
When in doubt, invoke the binary by absolute path.

triggers: test passes locally fails in ci timezone
date test off by hours ci
utc vs local time test fails
guides.title: Timezone difference breaks a build test
steps: Notice a date/time test fails only in CI, often by a whole-hour offset.
Compare your local timezone to the CI machine's (CI is usually UTC).
Make the test set a fixed timezone (e.g. force UTC) so it is deterministic everywhere.
Avoid comparing against 'now' or local-formatted dates; use explicit timezone-aware values.
Re-run locally with TZ set to UTC to reproduce, then confirm the fix.
Apply the same timezone discipline to the app code if it has the same bug.
tips: CI runs in UTC; your laptop probably does not — that gap is the off-by-hours bug.
Pin TZ in the test environment for reproducible date tests.

guides.title: Locale difference breaks the build
steps: Spot the symptom: different decimal separators, sort order, or month names than locally.
Check the CI machine's locale ('locale' command) versus yours.
Pin a locale for the build (e.g. set LANG/LC_ALL to a known value like C or en_US.UTF-8).
In code, format numbers and dates with explicit locale rather than the system default.
Re-run and confirm output matches across environments.
tips: String sorting and number formatting both shift with locale.
Setting LC_ALL=C gives the most predictable, locale-free behavior for tooling.

triggers: tests fail in ci depending on order
test passes alone fails in suite
guides.title: Tests are order-dependent in CI
steps: Run the failing test alone — if it passes solo, it depends on order or shared state.
Look for global state another test sets and does not clean up (env vars, singletons, files, db rows).
Add proper setup/teardown so each test starts clean.
Reproduce by running tests in a fixed seed/order the CI used.
Once isolated, re-run the whole suite repeatedly to confirm stability.
tips: Passing alone but failing in the suite screams shared mutable state.
Randomized test order surfaces these bugs early — keep it on.

triggers: unique constraint fails in parallel ci
guides.title: Parallel test workers collide on one database
steps: Confirm tests run in parallel and share a single database.
Look for failures like duplicate keys or rows another worker changed mid-test.
Give each worker its own database/schema, or wrap each test in a rolled-back transaction.
Avoid hardcoded fixed IDs; generate unique values per test.
Re-run in parallel and confirm no cross-worker interference.
tips: Per-worker databases are the cleanest isolation for parallel suites.
A rollback-per-test keeps the database pristine without recreating it.

triggers: no space left while caching build
docker build runs out of disk
guides.title: Build fails partway from a full disk
steps: Read the error for 'no space left' or write/copy failures.
Check free space on the build host ('df -h').
Find the big consumers (old caches, dangling docker images, build artifacts).
Add a cleanup step before the heavy build (prune images, clear stale caches).
If it is genuinely too big, use a larger runner or split the build.
Re-run and confirm the build completes.
tips: Dangling docker layers silently eat disk — prune them between builds.
A build that grows over time may need a bigger runner, not just cleanup.

triggers: javascript heap out of memory build
guides.title: Compiler killed (OOM) during build
steps: Spot the clue: 'killed', exit 137, or 'heap out of memory'.
Check the runner's memory and how much the build uses.
Lower memory pressure: reduce parallelism (fewer workers/threads at once).
For JS, raise the engine heap limit if appropriate, but prefer fixing the cause.
Split a giant build into smaller chunks or use a bigger runner.
Re-run and confirm it stays under the limit.
tips: Exit code 137 means the process was killed by the system, usually OOM.
More parallelism uses more memory — dial it down when the runner is small.

guides.title: CI cache key is too broad (restores stale deps)
steps: Notice old dependencies appear even after you changed the manifest.
Look at the cache key — if it is a fixed string, every run restores the same stale cache.
Include a hash of the lockfile in the cache key so it changes when deps change.
Add a restore-key fallback for partial hits, but the primary key should track the lockfile.
Clear the bad cache, re-run, and confirm fresh deps install when the lockfile changes.
tips: Key the cache on a hash of the lockfile — change deps, change key.
restore-keys give a warm-but-checked fallback without pinning you to stale content.

triggers: ci cache always cold never saved
cache not saved on failure ci
guides.title: CI cache never gets saved
steps: Check the job's end: caches usually save only when the job succeeds.
If the job fails before the save, fix the failure first or move caching earlier.
Confirm the path you cache actually exists at save time (print it).
Confirm the same key is used to save and restore.
Make a successful run, then a second run, and confirm the cache restores.
tips: A job that always fails will never populate a cache — green runs seed it.
Restore and save must use a matching key or you will always miss.

guides.title: Git submodule empty in CI checkout
steps: Notice a submodule folder exists but is empty in the build.
Remember a plain checkout does not pull submodules.
Tell the checkout to fetch submodules (submodules: recursive) or run 'git submodule update --init --recursive'.
If the submodule is private, provide credentials the checkout can use.
Re-run and confirm the submodule files are present.
tips: Submodules are opt-in for checkouts — they are skipped unless asked for.
Recursive handles submodules that themselves contain submodules.

triggers: ci builds whole monorepo every time
unrelated package changes trigger full build
guides.title: Monorepo CI rebuilds everything on any change
steps: Confirm a tiny change in one package triggers builds of all packages.
Add path filters so a workflow only runs when its package's files change.
For shared code, build only the affected packages plus their dependents.
Use the toolchain's affected-detection (it diffs against the base) instead of building all.
Re-run on a small change and confirm only the relevant package builds.
tips: Path filters cut wasted minutes on big repos.
'Affected' tooling computes the dependency graph so you rebuild only what matters.

triggers: css js not loading in production
guides.title: Static assets 404 after deploy
steps: Open the browser network tab and find the exact URL that 404s.
Compare that URL to where the build actually placed the file.
Check the configured public path / base URL matches the deploy location (e.g. served under a subpath).
Confirm the asset was included in the deployed bundle, not left in source only.
Fix the base path or output location and re-deploy.
Reload and confirm assets load with 200s.
tips: A wrong base path makes asset URLs point to the wrong place even though the file exists.
The network tab's failing URL tells you exactly what the browser expected.

triggers: direct url to page not found deployed
guides.title: SPA deep links 404 on reload after deploy
steps: Confirm the home page works but reloading a deep route 404s.
Understand the server looks for a real file at that path and does not find one.
Add a fallback so unknown paths serve index.html (the SPA then routes client-side).
Keep real files (assets, API) excluded from the fallback so they are served normally.
Re-deploy and reload a deep link to confirm it loads.
tips: The router lives in the browser; the server must hand it index.html for unknown paths.
Do not fallback API or asset routes — only app routes.

guides.title: CI YAML rejected for indentation/syntax
steps: Read the parser error — it usually gives a line and column.
Open that line and check indentation uses spaces, never tabs.
Confirm list items align and nested keys are indented consistently.
Watch for a missing colon, a value that needs quoting (':' or leading '*'), or a stray duplicate key.
Validate with a YAML linter before pushing.
Push the fixed file and confirm the workflow parses.
tips: YAML hates tabs — configure your editor to insert spaces.
Values containing ':' or starting with special characters must be quoted.

triggers: ci does not run on my changes
guides.title: Workflow does not trigger as expected
steps: Check the trigger config: which events, branches, and paths it listens for.
Confirm your push matches the branch filter (e.g. you pushed to a branch the filter excludes).
If path filters exist, confirm your changed files match them — they may exclude your folder.
Watch for 'paths-ignore' that accidentally swallows your change.
Adjust the filters, push again, and confirm the workflow starts.
tips: paths and paths-ignore are easy to get backwards — read them carefully.
A workflow on a default branch may not exist yet on your feature branch's history.

triggers: workflow only runs on main not branch
new workflow not running on feature branch
guides.title: Workflow seems to only run on the default branch
steps: Confirm the workflow file exists on the branch you pushed (it must be committed there).
Check the trigger's branch list includes feature branches or pull requests, not just main.
If it is a brand-new workflow, push it onto your branch so that branch has it.
For PR-based runs, open a PR so the pull_request event fires.
Re-push and confirm the run appears for your branch.
tips: A workflow only runs if it exists on the branch being built.
Add a pull_request trigger to get CI on branches before merge.

guides.title: Build output is not reproducible
steps: Build twice from the same source and diff the outputs to find what changes.
Common culprits: embedded timestamps, absolute paths, file ordering, and random IDs.
Pin a fixed build timestamp (e.g. SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH) so dates do not vary.
Sort file lists and avoid absolute paths in the output.
Pin tool versions so a minor update does not change bytes.
Build twice more and confirm identical hashes.
tips: Embedded build times are the most common reproducibility breaker.
Identical inputs should give identical bytes — chase every source of variation.

guides.title: Deploy briefly drops in-flight requests
steps: Confirm errors cluster exactly at deploy time, then clear.
Check that old instances stop receiving new traffic before they are killed (drain/connection draining on).
Make the app handle the shutdown signal and finish in-flight requests before exiting.
Ensure the new instance passes readiness before the old one is removed.
Add a small pre-stop delay so the load balancer notices the instance is leaving.
Re-deploy and confirm no error blip.
tips: Graceful shutdown means: stop accepting new, finish existing, then exit.
Readiness-before-removal is what makes a rolling deploy seamless.

triggers: rolled back code but db broken
guides.title: Code rollback breaks because the DB already migrated
steps: Recognize the trap: you reverted code, but the database schema is already on the new version.
Check whether the old code can run against the new schema (sometimes it can).
Prefer backward-compatible migrations so old and new code both work during transitions.
If you must revert schema, run a tested down-migration — and confirm no new data depends on it.
Going forward, deploy schema changes in two phases: add (compatible) first, remove later.
Verify the app runs after the rollback.
tips: Make migrations additive and backward-compatible so rollbacks stay safe.
Expand-then-contract: add the new shape, migrate, then remove the old shape in a later release.

guides.title: Package requires a different Node engine
steps: Read the 'unsupported engine' message naming the required range.
Check the Node version CI uses versus the required range.
Pin the build's Node version to one inside the range (a version file or the setup step).
Update your own engines field so contributors get the same version.
Reinstall with the right Node and confirm the warning/error clears.
tips: A version file checked into the repo keeps everyone on the same Node.
Engine ranges are a hint locally but can be enforced in CI.

triggers: syntax error feature not in python version
guides.title: CI uses the wrong Python version
steps: Print the active version: 'python --version' early in the job.
Compare it to what your code needs (a syntax/feature error is a strong hint).
Pin the version in the setup step (and in a version file like .python-version).
Recreate the virtualenv with that interpreter so installed packages match.
Re-run and confirm the version and the build are both correct.
tips: A 'SyntaxError' on valid new syntax means an old interpreter is running.
Match the venv's interpreter to the pinned version, not whatever is default.

guides.title: pip cannot resolve conflicting versions
steps: Read the resolver output — it names two requirements that cannot both be satisfied.
Identify which package pins the strict version causing the clash.
Loosen or update one requirement so a common version exists.
If a transitive dep is the problem, pin it explicitly to a version both accept.
Lock the resolved set ('pip freeze' or a lock tool) and commit it.
Reinstall from the lock to confirm a clean resolution.
tips: ResolutionImpossible means no single version satisfies everyone — something must move.
A committed lock file makes CI installs deterministic and fast.

triggers: pip building wheel from source slow
guides.title: pip builds from source because no wheel matches
steps: Notice pip says 'building wheel' and then needs a compiler.
Check whether a prebuilt wheel exists for your Python version, OS, and CPU arch.
If your platform is unusual (e.g. musl/Alpine or new arch), wheels may be missing.
Either install build tools to compile, or switch to a base image that has matching wheels.
Pin a package version that ships a wheel for your platform.
Reinstall and confirm it grabs a binary wheel.
tips: Alpine (musl) often lacks manylinux wheels — a slim Debian image avoids source builds.
Matching Python+OS+arch is what lets pip download a wheel instead of compiling.

triggers: docker script not running as command
guides.title: Docker entrypoint script will not execute
steps: Read the error: 'permission denied' or 'exec format error' on your script.
Make the script executable: 'chmod +x entrypoint.sh' and commit the mode.
Confirm the shebang line is correct and the file uses LF, not CRLF, line endings.
In the Dockerfile, RUN chmod +x on the script after COPY to be safe.
Use the exec form of ENTRYPOINT/CMD so signals pass through.
Rebuild and confirm the container starts.
tips: CRLF line endings make a shebang fail with a confusing 'no such file'.
Set the executable bit in git or with a RUN chmod in the image.

guides.title: CRLF line endings break a shell script
steps: Spot tell-tale errors like '\r: command not found' or 'bad interpreter'.
Recognize the file has Windows CRLF line endings inside a Linux build.
Convert the file to LF (dos2unix, or your editor's line-ending setting).
Add a .gitattributes rule forcing LF for shell scripts so it cannot regress.
Re-commit and rebuild; the script should run cleanly.
tips: A trailing \r turns 'bash' into 'bash\r', which does not exist.
Pin '*.sh text eol=lf' in .gitattributes to lock it in.

guides.title: CI jobs stuck pending (no runner/minutes)
steps: Check whether jobs are 'queued/pending' rather than 'failing'.
Look at your account's usage — you may be out of included minutes.
Confirm a runner label your job requests actually exists and is online (self-hosted runners can be offline).
If self-hosted, restart/register the runner; if hosted, free up minutes or switch runner type.
Re-run and confirm a runner picks the job up.
tips: Pending forever usually means no eligible runner, not a code bug.
A job requesting a label no runner has will wait indefinitely.

triggers: weird errors only fixed by no cache
guides.title: A poisoned cache breaks the build
steps: Notice the build only succeeds after clearing the cache.
Identify which cache is involved (deps, build, compiler).
Delete/invalidate that cache once to get green.
Find why bad content got cached — usually a key that does not change when inputs do.
Improve the cache key so changed inputs produce a new key.
Re-run twice to confirm cached runs stay correct.
tips: If clearing the cache always fixes it, the cache key is too loose.
Cache content keyed on input hashes cannot go stale silently.

triggers: env var cut off at newline
guides.title: Multiline secret gets truncated in env
steps: Confirm the broken value is multiline (a private key or certificate).
Check the length in the target ('echo ${#KEY}') against the original length.
If it is short, the newlines were lost or it was split at the first line.
Store the multiline value safely (base64-encode it, or use a file-based secret).
If base64, decode it back to a file at startup.
Verify the decoded value matches the original and the app accepts it.
tips: Newlines in env vars are fragile — base64 makes the value a single safe line.
A file-mounted secret avoids newline mangling entirely.

triggers: file ignored by gitignore needed in build
required file not committed because ignored
guides.title: A required file is hidden by .gitignore
steps: Confirm the build needs a file that is missing in CI.
Run 'git check-ignore -v path' to see which .gitignore rule excludes it.
Decide: should it be committed (then add a '!' exception) or generated at build time?
If it is a real config the build needs and is not secret, add it with an exception line.
If it is secret, provide it via a secret/env instead, not in git.
Re-run and confirm the build sees the file.
tips: git check-ignore tells you exactly which line is hiding a file.
Secrets should never be committed even with an exception — inject them at runtime.

triggers: step output empty in next step ci
cannot read previous step output ci
guides.title: Step/job output not received downstream
steps: Confirm the producing step actually wrote an output (print it right after).
Check you used the official output mechanism (write to the outputs file), not a plain shell variable.
Reference it with the correct step/job id and output name downstream.
For job-level outputs, declare the job's outputs and 'needs' it from the consumer.
Re-run and print the received value to confirm it arrives.
tips: Shell variables vanish between steps — use the outputs file to share them.
Job outputs must be declared on the job and the consumer must 'needs' it.

guides.title: Build artifact/image is too large
steps: Measure the size and find the biggest contributors (image layer sizes or bundle analyzer).
For images, use a multi-stage build so only the runtime files ship, not the toolchain.
Switch to a slim base image and avoid installing dev tools in the final stage.
Remove caches and temp files in the same layer they are created.
For bundles, drop unused dependencies and enable tree-shaking/minification.
Rebuild and confirm a smaller size.
tips: Multi-stage builds keep compilers out of the final image.
Cleaning files in a later layer does not shrink the image — clean within the same RUN.

triggers: new domain not resolving after deploy
guides.title: DNS change has not propagated after deploy
steps: Resolve the domain directly ('dig' or 'nslookup') and compare to the IP you set.
If it still shows the old IP, the change has not propagated or TTL is high.
Check the record's TTL — high TTL means caches hold the old value longer.
Query an authoritative/public resolver to see the new value at the source.
Wait out the TTL or flush local DNS cache, then recheck.
Confirm the domain resolves to the new target.
tips: TTL is how long resolvers cache the old answer — lower it before planned changes.
Querying the authoritative server shows the truth, bypassing intermediate caches.

guides.title: TLS certificate expired in production
steps: Confirm the symptom: browser security warning or handshake errors.
Check the certificate's expiry ('openssl s_client' or browser cert view).
If expired, renew it (or fix auto-renewal that silently failed).
Confirm the renewed cert is actually installed and the server reloaded it.
Verify the full chain is served, not just the leaf, so clients trust it.
Reload and confirm a valid, trusted certificate.
tips: Automate renewal and alert before expiry — manual renewal always gets forgotten.
A missing intermediate chain makes some clients reject an otherwise-valid cert.

guides.title: A secret leaked into build logs
steps: Stop and treat the secret as compromised — rotate it immediately.
Find the step that printed it (often a debug 'env' dump or 'set -x' tracing).
Remove that print and disable command tracing around secret use.
Ensure secrets are registered as masked so CI redacts them if printed again.
Purge or restrict access to the logs that contain it if possible.
Re-run with the new secret and confirm nothing sensitive prints.
tips: Rotate first — masking the log later does not un-leak a value people saw.
'set -x' echoes commands including secrets; turn it off around sensitive lines.

triggers: ci passes then fails on self hosted
guides.title: Self-hosted runner keeps dirty state
steps: Suspect this when builds pass on fresh runners but flake on a self-hosted one.
Remember self-hosted runners reuse the same machine, so leftover files/processes persist.
Clean the workspace at the start of the job (remove untracked files, reset state).
Kill leftover background processes and free ports from prior runs.
Consider ephemeral runners (fresh per job) if pollution keeps happening.
Re-run repeatedly to confirm stability.
tips: Hosted runners are fresh each time; self-hosted are not — clean up explicitly.
Ephemeral runners trade a little speed for guaranteed clean state.

triggers: import works in dev fails when packaged
module not found in built package
guides.title: Imports work in dev but break when packaged
steps: Reproduce by installing the built package into a clean environment and importing it.
Check the package manifest includes all needed modules/data files (not just the obvious .py files).
Confirm non-code data (templates, json) is declared as package data so it ships.
Fix the packaging config to include the missing files.
Rebuild, reinstall into the clean env, and import again to confirm.
Run a tiny smoke test from the installed package, not the source tree.
tips: Running from source hides packaging gaps — always test the installed artifact.
Data files need explicit inclusion; they are not shipped automatically.

triggers: deployed an old commit by mistake
production running different code than expected
guides.title: Wrong artifact promoted to production
steps: Find what commit/version is actually running (print it from a build-stamped value).
Compare it to the commit you intended to deploy.
Trace the promotion step — it may pin a fixed tag or 'latest' that points elsewhere.
Use immutable, content/commit-tagged artifacts so each deploy is unambiguous.
Re-promote the correct artifact by its exact identifier.
Confirm the running version matches the intended commit.
tips: 'latest' is a moving target — promote by exact immutable tag/digest.
Stamp the build with its commit so production can tell you what it is.

triggers: cannot merge required check not run
branch protection waiting for check that never runs
merge blocked on a check that does not exist
guides.title: Merge blocked by a required check that never runs
steps: Read the merge block — it names a required status check.
Check whether a job by that exact name actually runs on PRs.
A renamed or path-filtered job can disappear, leaving the required name unmet forever.
Either make the job run (and report that name) on every PR, or update the required-checks list to the new name.
If a job is skipped by a path filter, configure it to report a neutral success instead of nothing.
Re-open/re-run the PR and confirm the check reports.
tips: A required check that never runs is an unmergeable PR — names must match exactly.
Skipped jobs report nothing; required checks want a result, so emit a pass when skipped.

guides.title: Build broke with no code change (tool drift)
steps: Confirm nothing in your code changed since the last green build.
Suspect a floating dependency or tool version that auto-updated.
Compare tool versions between the last green run and the now-red run (check setup logs).
Pin the tool/action/base-image to the version that worked.
Add lockfiles/pins so future runs are reproducible.
Re-run and confirm green, then upgrade deliberately later.
tips: 'It broke with no change' almost always means an unpinned dependency moved.
Pinning by exact version (or digest) makes builds time-proof.

triggers: users see old page after deploy cdn
guides.title: CDN caches HTML and serves stale pages
steps: Confirm the origin has the new HTML but users get the old one.
Check the CDN cache headers on the HTML response.
Set HTML to no-cache/short TTL while assets stay long-cached (they are hashed).
Invalidate the CDN cache for the HTML paths after deploy.
Reload with cache disabled and confirm the new HTML.
Automate the invalidation as part of the deploy.
tips: Cache hashed assets forever, but keep the HTML entry point short-lived.
A post-deploy purge of HTML paths prevents the stale-page trap.

triggers: default value wins over env ci
guides.title: A default value overrides the env variable
steps: Print the resolved config value at startup to see what actually won.
Trace the precedence: a hardcoded default may be applied after the env read.
Confirm the env variable name matches exactly (case and spelling).
Confirm the variable is actually set in the target environment (not just locally).
Fix the order so env overrides defaults, and re-deploy.
Confirm the startup log shows the env value winning.
tips: Read env once, then fall back to a default — not the other way around.
A typo'd variable name silently falls through to the default.

triggers: cannot connect to docker daemon ci
guides.title: Docker commands fail inside CI
steps: Read the error: 'cannot connect to the Docker daemon' means no daemon/socket access.
Confirm the CI job has Docker available (a Docker service or daemon enabled).
If using Docker-in-Docker, ensure the service is started and the socket is reachable.
Check the runner user has permission to the docker socket.
Use the CI's recommended way to build images (a build action or a privileged service).
Re-run a 'docker info' step to confirm connectivity before the real build.
tips: A quick 'docker info' step proves daemon access before the heavy build runs.
Building images often needs a special service or privileged mode in CI.

guides.title: Path-too-long error on a Windows build
steps: Read the error pointing at a long file path.
Recognize Windows has a default max path length that deep node_modules/build trees can exceed.
Enable long-path support on the runner (registry/group policy) if you control it.
Shorten the checkout directory so the total path is shorter.
Enable git's long-path support ('git config core.longpaths true').
Re-run and confirm files create successfully.
tips: Deeply nested dependency folders are the usual cause on Windows.
A shorter base checkout path buys a lot of headroom under the limit.

triggers: app sleeps then errors first hit
guides.title: Cold start times out the first request
steps: Notice the first request after idle is slow or times out, then it is fine.
Recognize the instance scaled to zero and must boot on the first hit.
Increase the request timeout to cover boot time, or set a minimum of one warm instance.
Trim startup work (lazy-load heavy things) so boot is faster.
Add a warmup ping or readiness gate so traffic waits for boot.
Re-test a cold request and confirm it succeeds.
tips: Scale-to-zero saves money but trades a cold-start delay.
Keeping one warm instance removes the cold start for a small cost.

triggers: env var works lowercase fails uppercase
guides.title: Env var name case mismatch
steps: Compare the exact name the code reads against the name you set.
Remember env var names are case-sensitive on Linux (MYVAR != myvar).
Make both sides use the same casing (convention is UPPER_SNAKE_CASE).
Print the value at startup to confirm it is read.
Re-deploy and confirm the variable resolves.
tips: Stick to UPPER_SNAKE_CASE for env vars to avoid case surprises.
Linux is case-sensitive even though Windows often is not.

triggers: tests connect before db ready ci
db not up when tests run
guides.title: Tests run before the DB service is ready
steps: Spot 'connection refused' right at the start of the test job.
Recognize the database service container takes a moment to accept connections.
Add a wait-for-ready loop (poll the port/health) before running tests.
Prefer the service's built-in health check and 'needs healthy' if your CI supports it.
Re-run and confirm tests start only after the DB is reachable.
tips: A started container is not the same as a ready-to-accept-connections one.
A health check plus dependency ordering beats a fixed sleep.

triggers: ci red because of audit vulnerability
guides.title: Security audit fails the build unexpectedly
steps: Read which advisory and package triggered the failure.
Decide if it is reachable in your usage or a transitive dev-only dependency.
Update the affected package to a fixed version if one exists.
If no fix yet, document and temporarily set the audit to warn (not fail) for that advisory.
Re-run install/audit and confirm it passes or only warns.
Track the advisory so you upgrade when a fix lands.
tips: Not every advisory is exploitable in your code — assess reachability.
Prefer fixing over silencing; only suppress with a clear note and follow-up.

triggers: app fails writing temp file deploy
guides.title: App fails writing to a read-only filesystem
steps: Read the error: 'read-only file system' or write permission denied.
Recognize many container/serverless runtimes mount the app filesystem read-only.
Find what the app tries to write (logs, cache, temp files, uploads).
Redirect writes to a writable temp dir or a mounted writable volume.
For persistent data, use external storage (object store/db), not local disk.
Re-deploy and confirm no write failures.
tips: Treat container disks as ephemeral and mostly read-only.
Use the designated temp directory for scratch files, external storage for anything that must persist.

guides.title: A workflow triggers itself in a loop
steps: Notice runs spawning back-to-back from commits the workflow itself makes.
Recognize a job that pushes a commit can re-trigger the on-push workflow.
Add a guard: skip the workflow when the commit author is the automation, or add '[skip ci]' to those commits.
Alternatively use a token that does not re-trigger workflows for bot pushes.
Re-run once and confirm the loop stops.
tips: Automated commits can chase their own tail — guard the trigger.
'[skip ci]' in the commit message is a simple circuit breaker.

triggers: test fixture write fails in build
guides.title: Tests write to a non-writable location
steps: Find where the failing test writes and the permission error it hits.
Recognize the test assumes a writable working directory that CI may not grant.
Point test file writes at a temp directory created per test.
Clean up created files in teardown so they do not leak between tests.
Re-run in CI and confirm the writes succeed.
tips: Use a fresh temp directory per test instead of writing into the repo.
Per-test temp dirs also fix order-dependent failures from leftover files.

triggers: scheduled job runs twice after scaling
two instances both run the task
singleton task runs on every replica
guides.title: A 'once' task runs on every replica
steps: Notice a scheduled/startup task fires multiple times after scaling up.
Recognize every replica runs the same code, so per-instance tasks duplicate.
Move the task to a single place: a dedicated scheduler, a leader-elected instance, or an external cron.
Add a lock so only one instance performs the work at a time.
Make the task idempotent so a rare double-run does no harm.
Re-deploy at scale and confirm it runs once.
tips: Every replica is identical — 'run on startup' means 'run N times' at N replicas.
A distributed lock or external scheduler turns N runs into one.

guides.title: .env loaded in dev but not in production
steps: Confirm the app relies on a .env file that exists locally but not in production.
Recognize many setups only auto-load .env in development, by design.
Provide the same variables through the platform's real environment/secret settings.
Do not ship the .env file itself to production (it should not be committed).
Print the resolved values (names/lengths, not secrets) on boot to confirm.
Re-deploy with the platform-set variables and verify.
tips: .env is a dev convenience; production should use real environment configuration.
Never commit .env — provide the values through the platform's secrets.

triggers: third party action changed behavior ci
guides.title: A third-party action moved under a floating tag
steps: Suspect this when a previously-green pipeline breaks with no repo change.
Check which external actions you reference and how they are pinned.
If pinned to a branch or major tag, the action could have changed under you.
Pin actions to a specific version or, better, a commit digest for immutability.
Re-run and confirm green, then upgrade the pin deliberately when ready.
Read the action's changelog before bumping.
tips: Pinning to @main means you run whatever they pushed last — risky.
A commit-digest pin is the strongest guarantee of reproducibility.

triggers: links broken when hosted in subfolder
guides.title: App broken when hosted under a subpath
steps: Confirm the app is served under a path like /app, not the root.
Notice asset and link URLs point at the root and 404.
Set the build's base path/public path to the subpath it is served from.
Rebuild so generated URLs include the subpath.
Re-deploy and reload; assets and links should resolve.
Make the base path configurable so the same build can move.
tips: Root-relative URLs break under a subpath — set the base path at build time.
A configurable base lets one build serve from / or /app.

triggers: test fails calling external api ci
flaky test depends on external service
guides.title: A test depends on the live internet
steps: Notice the test fails with network/timeout errors only in CI.
Recognize CI may block outbound network or the external service is flaky.
Mock or stub the external call so the test does not touch the network.
If integration coverage is needed, isolate those tests and run them separately with explicit network access.
Re-run the unit tests offline to confirm they pass without network.
tips: Unit tests should never hit the real internet — mock the boundary.
Keep slow/network integration tests in a separate, opt-in job.

triggers: container takes long to stop deploy
guides.title: App ignores SIGTERM and is force-killed
steps: Notice the container takes the full grace period then gets force-killed on deploy.
Recognize the platform sends SIGTERM first; if ignored, it sends SIGKILL after a timeout.
Make the app handle SIGTERM: stop accepting work and finish in-flight tasks.
Use the exec form in Docker so signals reach the app (not a shell wrapper that swallows them).
Confirm the process is PID 1 or that signals are forwarded to it.
Re-deploy and confirm a fast, clean shutdown.
tips: The shell form of CMD can eat SIGTERM — use the exec form so PID 1 is your app.
A handled SIGTERM is the difference between a graceful and a violent shutdown.

triggers: ci green but no tests ran
guides.title: CI is green but ran zero tests
steps: Read the test summary — '0 tests' or 'no tests collected' is a false green.
Check the test discovery path/pattern; it may not match your test files.
Confirm the runner is pointed at the right folder and naming convention.
Add a guard that fails the job if zero tests are collected.
Fix the path/pattern so tests are found.
Re-run and confirm the real test count is non-zero.
tips: Zero collected tests passing is the most dangerous green there is.
Make 'no tests found' an explicit failure so it never sneaks by.

triggers: app cannot reach database different region
slow or failing connection wrong region
guides.title: Deployed app is in the wrong region for its resources
steps: Note slow or failing connections to the database/cache after deploy.
Check the region of the app versus the region of its dependencies.
If they differ, the latency or network rules can break or slow connections.
Move the app to the same region as its data, or vice versa.
Confirm firewall/network rules allow the app's region to reach the resource.
Re-deploy and confirm fast, working connections.
tips: Cross-region hops add latency and sometimes block on network rules.
Keep an app close to its primary data store.

triggers: local env var leaks into build
my shell variable changes build behavior
build behaves differently per machine env
guides.title: A stray local env var changes the build
steps: Reproduce by running the build in a clean shell with a minimal environment.
Diff your shell's environment against a teammate's or CI's.
Find a variable the build reads that you set locally but CI does not (or vice versa).
Make the build set what it needs explicitly instead of inheriting ambient values.
Document required variables so all environments match.
Re-run clean and confirm consistent behavior.
tips: 'Works on my machine' often means your shell secretly sets a variable.
A clean-shell build reveals hidden environmental dependencies.

triggers: ci tests a merge commit not my code
checked out merge ref ci confusing
ci sha not my latest commit
guides.title: PR CI tests a merge commit, not your HEAD
steps: Notice the CI commit SHA differs from your latest pushed commit.
Recognize many systems test a temporary merge of your branch into the base.
This is usually good — it tests the post-merge state — but can surprise you if the base moved.
If a failure seems unrelated, rebase/merge the latest base and re-run.
To debug exactly your commit, configure the checkout to use your HEAD ref instead of the merge ref.
Re-run and reconcile the difference.
tips: Testing the merge result catches conflicts with a moving base early.
If the base changed, your green branch can still fail the merged build.

guides.title: A partial/incomplete artifact got published
steps: Confirm the published artifact is missing files or is truncated.
Trace the order: the publish step may run even when the build step failed or is unfinished.
Make publish depend on a fully successful build (proper job ordering / 'needs').
Publish atomically: build to a temp name, then move/promote only on success.
Re-run, fail a build on purpose, and confirm nothing publishes.
Re-publish the complete artifact.
tips: Publish only after a confirmed-complete build, never alongside it.
Atomic promote (temp then swap) prevents half-written releases.

triggers: ansi color codes break log parser ci
color codes in build logs cause failure
guides.title: ANSI color codes break a log parser
steps: Spot stray escape sequences (like '[0;32m') in captured output.
Recognize a tool emits colors because it thinks it talks to a terminal.
Tell the tool to disable color (a --no-color flag or NO_COLOR env var) in CI.
Or set the tool to detect non-TTY and turn color off automatically.
Re-run and confirm clean, parseable text output.
tips: NO_COLOR=1 disables color for many well-behaved tools.
Colors are for humans at a terminal — turn them off for machines parsing logs.

triggers: too many connections database after deploy
each instance opens too many connections
guides.title: DB connection limit hit after scaling deploy
steps: Read the error: the database refuses new connections at its limit.
Count connections: instances times pool size can exceed the database max.
Lower each instance's pool size so total stays under the limit.
Add a connection pooler in front of the database to multiplex.
Make sure connections are released/closed and not leaked.
Re-deploy and watch connection counts stay safe.
tips: Total connections = replicas times pool size — do the math before scaling.
A pooler lets many app instances share a small number of DB connections.

triggers: link points to wrong place after clone
guides.title: A symlink breaks in the build
steps: Notice a path that is a symlink resolves to nothing in CI.
Check whether the checkout preserved symlinks (some setups/zip steps do not).
Confirm the link target is committed and the relative path is correct from the link's location.
On Windows runners, symlink support may be off — enable it or avoid symlinks.
Replace fragile symlinks with a copy or a build step if portability matters.
Re-run and confirm the link resolves.
tips: Zipping/unzipping artifacts can turn symlinks into broken stubs.
Windows needs symlink support enabled; otherwise avoid them in cross-platform builds.

triggers: staging secret used in production deploy
guides.title: Deploy used the wrong environment's secrets
steps: Confirm which environment the deploy job targeted.
Check that environment-scoped secrets are attached to the right environment.
Look for a global secret with the same name shadowing the environment one.
Make the deploy job select the correct environment so its scoped secrets apply.
Re-deploy and verify the app authenticated against the intended environment.
Print the target environment name on boot to confirm.
tips: Scope secrets per environment and select the environment in the deploy job.
A same-named global secret can quietly override a scoped one.

triggers: tests fail missing built file ci
test needs build output not present
guides.title: Tests run before the build that produces what they need
steps: Find the missing file the test imports or reads.
Confirm it is a build output (compiled/generated), not committed source.
Check job/step ordering — the build that creates it must run first.
Add the build step before the test step (or 'needs' the build job).
If tests and build are separate jobs, pass the output as an artifact.
Re-run in order and confirm the test finds its dependency.
tips: Generated files do not exist until a build step makes them.
Across jobs, share build outputs via artifacts, not assumptions.

triggers: app logs to file not visible deploy
guides.title: Production logs missing (written to a file)
steps: Confirm logs are nowhere in the platform's log view.
Check whether the app writes to a log file instead of stdout/stderr.
Recognize containers/platforms collect logs from stdout/stderr, not random files.
Configure the app to log to stdout/stderr.
Re-deploy and confirm logs appear in the platform dashboard.
Use the platform's log retention/forwarding for storage.
tips: The Twelve-Factor rule: treat logs as a stream to stdout, not files.
A file on an ephemeral disk vanishes with the container.

triggers: timing test passes locally fails ci
race in test depends on sleep
guides.title: A timing test is flaky on slow CI
steps: Notice the test passes locally but flakes on a slower CI machine.
Spot reliance on a fixed sleep or wall-clock timing.
Replace fixed sleeps with waiting on a condition (poll until ready, with a generous timeout).
For time logic, inject a fake clock instead of using real time.
Re-run the test many times in CI to confirm it is stable.
Remove the brittle sleep entirely.
tips: CI machines are often slower and noisier — fixed sleeps are a coin flip there.
Wait-for-condition beats sleep; a fake clock beats real time.

triggers: image tag changed under same name
latest tag points to different image
cannot reproduce old deploy tag moved
guides.title: A registry tag was overwritten
steps: Notice the same tag now pulls different content than before.
Recognize mutable tags (like 'latest' or a version you re-pushed) can be overwritten.
Pin deploys to the image digest (sha256), which is immutable, not the tag.
Record the digest of each deploy so you can reproduce or roll back exactly.
Stop re-pushing the same tag; publish a new unique tag per build.
Re-deploy by digest and confirm reproducibility.
tips: Tags move; digests do not — deploy by digest for true immutability.
Recording the deployed digest makes rollback exact, not approximate.

triggers: tool missing because setup cached skip
setup step skipped due to cache ci
guides.title: A setup step got skipped, leaving a tool missing
steps: Find the step that should install a tool and check if it actually ran.
Look for a condition (cache hit / 'if') that skipped the install.
Confirm the cache it trusted actually contains the tool — a stale or empty cache plus a skip leaves nothing.
Either remove the over-eager skip or verify the cache before trusting it.
Add a post-setup check ('tool --version') that fails fast if missing.
Re-run and confirm the tool is present.
tips: A 'skip install if cached' shortcut breaks when the cache is empty but the condition says hit.
A version check right after setup catches a missing tool immediately.
